title: Spring-Ford marching band wins its first national championship
summary: The 82-member Golden Rams Marching Band took the USBands Group III Open Class national title at MetLife Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, scoring a season-high 94.25 and earning the Best Music caption. It is the first national championship in school history and follows a state title earlier this fall.

title: Ursinus lands $500,000 federal grant for student mental health
summary: A four-year suicide prevention grant from the federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration will pay for a full-time student well-being specialist, a 24-hour support service and a scholarship fund covering off-campus therapy and rides to appointments. The college is calling the effort the SAFE Initiative.
loc: Ursinus College, 601 E. Main St., Collegeville

title: Historical society opens an exhibit on 22 years of the Firebird Festival
summary: The new show at the Historical Society of the Phoenixville Area museum traces the festival from its 2004 start with design models, videos, fired clay birds and memorabilia, including the 2014 year when vandals burned the bird early and volunteers rebuilt it in days. This year's Firebird Festival is Dec. 12 at Reservoir Park.

title: Costumed teams push beds down Third Avenue for two homeless shelters
summary: The ninth annual Phoenixville Bed Races sent five-person teams, four pushers and a helmeted rider, down Third Avenue at Reeves Park and back over the weekend, with prizes for fastest bed, best theme and most money raised. Proceeds go to Ann's Heart and Good Samaritan Services toward a $20,000 goal, and donations are still open.

title: Kolka steps down after 12 seasons as Owen J. Roberts football coach
summary: Rich Kolka resigned after the Wildcats' season ended last Friday, leaving with an 82-49 record, the best winning percentage of any head coach in school history, and the program's first two District 1 playoff wins in 2024 and 2025. He plans to stay on as coach of OJR's girls' flag football team.
loc: Owen J. Roberts High School, Bucktown

title: Every Phoenixville school joins a hunger relief drive Nov. 16-20
summary: For Hunger and Homelessness Awareness Week, each school in the Phoenixville Area School District will run its own food collection or fundraiser for Ann's Heart, Phoenixville Area Community Services, the Chester County Food Bank and the district's Phantom Family Fund. Hares Hill Elementary is raising money for the fund, which covers emergency housing, food and clothing for district families year-round.

title: Volunteer orchestra gives a flute and piano concerto its world premiere Nov. 22
summary: The Providence Chamber Orchestra will debut Nina Siniakova's As We Were Gazing at the Stars at 4 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 22, at St. John's Lutheran Church, with the composer at the piano and Belgian flutist Berten D'Hollander. Works by Lyadov and Dvorak fill out the program; admission is free, with a suggested $10 donation.
loc: St. John's Lutheran Church, 355 St. John's Circle, Phoenixville

title: Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and 122 Toll townhomes fill out the District at Black Rock
summary: The mixed-use project rising on the old Quest Diagnostics campus at 1201 S. Collegeville Road is 89 percent pre-leased as construction starts, with Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and Barnes & Noble anchoring more than 148,000 square feet of retail alongside J. Crew, Sephora and Shake Shack. Toll Brothers bought an adjacent 7.3 acres for 122 townhomes, and the center is slated to finish in late 2027.
loc: 1201 S. Collegeville Road, Upper Providence Township

title: Private club proposed for residential block of Gay Street goes to zoning board Nov. 18
summary: The 1978 Phoenix Foundation is asking the Zoning Hearing Board for a special exception to run a private club and community center, plus a variance for office use, at 315 Gay St. in the Residential Infill District. The hearing is 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Borough Hall, and the application can be inspected there.

title: Chicken Salad Chick sets Nov. 18 opening at Providence Town Center
summary: The Southern fast-casual chain's first Philadelphia-area restaurant takes the former Z!Eats space and will seat 55, with free chicken salad for a year promised to the first 100 guests. The local franchise group plans six locations across Montgomery and Chester counties.
loc: 500 Broad St., Providence Town Center, Collegeville
